# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-29 (Extended v198)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Champs-Élysées, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby.

Paris sewer system: 5,300 fathoms in 1663; 40,300 metres by 1 January 1832; follows street layout (2,200 streets); ridge divides waters to Seine or Grand Sewer; Sainte-Avoye sewer marks watershed culmination. Grand Sewer (old brook of Ménilmontant) terminates blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant knoll. No direct communication with Amelot sewer branch. Belt sewer has single outlet. **Fontis phenomenon** (dangerous water-saturated ground): Depth varies 3-4 to 8-10+ feet; discard loads to escape; death slow if earth predominates, prompt if water predominates. **Champs-Élysées quagmire**: Common obstacle; 1836 Faubourg Saint-Honoré sewer reconstruction took six months due to quicksand. **Sewer outlet design flaw (Chapter 29)**: Pointed arch vault narrows funnel-like, lower than main gallery—faulty penitentiary-inspired wicket design (later corrected). Heavy grating at river outlet, double-locked with rust-caked lock, rarely swung hinges, iron staple sunk deep. Beyond: open air, daylight, shore (Grand-Caillou—solitary point), distant quays, bridge of Jéna (downstream), bridge of Invalides (upstream). Flies enter/exit through bars.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7).

**Confirmed rumor (Chapter 29)**: In letter Yera Haskick burned after reading, Yera Stenworth revealed fire at Dunstead granary set on purpose.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate lodgings. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work, moved there (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate lodgings (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest (Chapter 28). Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7, Chapter 28). Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month (Chapter 28). Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven (Chapter 28). Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford (Chapter 28). Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate (Chapter 29). **Gadrek Prydenridge married eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on (Chapter 29)**.

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with Cosette memory. **Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Barricade, Sewer Escape, and Emergence (Chapters 24-29)

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar; grief surpassed bounds.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman and officer, smashed helmet. Stared silently. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting, caring. Reappeared in intervals. Nothing resembling blow or personal defence from his hands. Held peace, lent succor. Received few scratches only. Meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: After final collapse, Valjean found himself trapped behind small wall near Rue de la Petite Truanderie. Discovered iron grating about two feet square beneath loose paving-stones, leading to dark aperture. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted inert Marius onto shoulders, descended into well with elbows and knees three metres below surface, dropped grating behind.

**Sewer journey (6th June, after barricade)**: Escaped via Paris sewer system. Cautiously advanced, fearing hole/sink/gulf; discovered paving continued. After fifty paces, passage terminated; two ways presented. Chose based on slope. Thought probably in sewer des Halles; better plunge into labyrinth than risk daylight capture between Pont au Change and Pont-Neuf. **Water flow changed direction**: Gradually perceived water beating against heels instead of toes. Sewer began descending toward belt sewer, not Seine. Ridge forms watershed; Valjean reached culminating point, directed course toward belt sewer. **Branch encounters**: Every encounter with branch felt its angles; avoided narrower ways terminating in blind alleys, correctly judging by physical sense. Avoided quadruple trap—four labyrinths set in darkness. **Police patrol (6th June)**: Prefect Gisquet ordered battue of sewers. Three squads explored subterranean drain. One patrol explored curving gallery and three blind alleys beneath Rue du Cadran. While passing lantern, Valjean perceived entrance to gallery narrower than principal passage, did not penetrate, passed on. Patrol, emerging from Cadran gallery, fancied they heard footsteps in direction of belt sewer—actually Valjean's steps. Sergeant raised lantern, squad gazed into mist. Valjean hugged wall and halted. Lack of sleep, food, emotions caused him pass into state of visionary. **Patrol's decision**: At crossroads "de service" in Montmartre sewer, patrol whispered together. Concluded they had been mistaken, no noise, useless to entangle in belt sewer, ought hasten toward Saint-Merry; if anything to do, in that quarter. Patrol resumed march, leaving Valjean behind. **Sergeant's discharge**: Before departure, sergeant discharged gun in direction of Valjean. Ball struck arch over his head. Had patrol not been forbidden to separate by prefecture instructions, Jean Valjean would have been captured.

**Fontis encounter (Chapter 29)**: Caused by downpour preceding day. Pavement, badly sustained by subjacent sand, gave way, produced stoppage of water. Valjean felt pavement vanishing beneath feet, entered slime. Water on surface, slime at bottom. Could not retrace steps—Marius dying, Jean Valjean exhausted. Sank until only head above water, two arms holding up Marius. Turned face rearward to escape water, breathe. At supreme moment, struck something solid—fragment of vaulting, partly submerged but solid, curved inclined plane. Well-built pavements form vault, possess firmness. Once on this plane, he was safe. Mounted inclined plane, reached other side of quagmire.

**Post-fontis state and continuation**: Although had not left life in fontis, seemed to have left strength behind. Supreme effort exhausted him. Obliged to pause for breath every three or four steps. Once forced to seat himself on banquette. But energy persisted. Rose again, walked desperately, proceeded hundred paces almost without drawing breath, suddenly came in contact with wall. Reached elbow of sewer, arrived at turn, struck wall with head. Raised eyes, at extremity of vault, perceived light. Daylight. Jean Valjean saw the outlet.

**Outlet and entrapment (Chapter 29)**: Pointed arch, lower than vault, gradually narrowed like funnel interior. Light went early, as it did that time of year. Valjean no longer conscious of fatigue, no longer felt Marius' weight, found legs of steel, ran rather than walked. Approached outlet, became more distinctly defined. Laid Marius down along wall, on dry portion of vaulting. Went to grating, clenched fists round bars, gave frenzied shock—did not move. Seized bars one after another, hoping to tear away least solid and use as lever or break lock. Not a bar stirred. Teeth of tiger not more firmly fixed. No lever; no prying possible. Obstacle invincible. No means of opening gate. Beyond grating: open air, river, daylight, shore (narrow but sufficient for escape), distant quays, Paris, gulf in which one so easily hides, broad horizon, liberty. Bridge of Jéna discernible downstream, bridge of Invalides upstream. Most solitary point in Paris. Flies entering/exiting through bars. Valjean laid Marius down, then fell upon pavement beside Marius (still made no movement), head bent between knees. This was last drop of anguish. They both caught in immense, gloomy web of death.

**Thénardier's appearance (Chapter 29)**: Jean Valjean, accustomed to alarms, steeled to unforeseen shocks, instantly regained possession of his presence of mind. Thénardier emerged from darkness. Raising right hand to forehead, formed shade, screwed up eyes, characterizing sagacious attention of man endeavoring to recognize another man. Did not succeed initially—Valjean had back turned to light, disfigured, bemired, bleeding. But illuminated by cellar light from grating, livid yet precise, Thénardier immediately "leaped into" Valjean's eyes. Inequality of conditions assure advantage to Valjean in mysterious duel about to begin. Encounter between Valjean veiled and Thénardier unmasked.

**Thénardier's proposition (Chapter 29)**: "I'm asking you questions, but you're perfectly right not to answer. It's an apprenticeship against that cursed quarter of an hour before the examining magistrate. And then, when you don't talk at all, you run no risk of talking too loud. That's no matter, as I can't see your face and as I don't know your name, you are wrong in supposing that I don't know who you are and what you want. I twig. You've broken up that gentleman a bit; now you want to tuck him away somewhere. The river, that great hider of folly, is what you want. I'll get you out of your scrape. Helping a good fellow in a pinch is what suits me to a hair." Thénardier advises body disposed in river better than sewer—river belongs to everybody, true grave, carrion after month, no inquiry, workmen tomorrow would discover body in sewer, prompt police pursuit, Valjean done well considering such matters.

## Year 8 (Spring) Seasonal Observations
Rain threatened since morning but held off. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Baker's boy late again. Light went early. Kassa complained of aching back. Kassa counted coins twice, came up penny short. Price of salt scandal. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Wind came off water with salt and tar smell. Dogs barked at nothing. Havie and Ilrald Prydenridge watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly. Nerine and Gadrek discussed price of salt. Luvie remarked river up again, Yera said always was in spring. Lurald Stenworth fell asleep before fire caught. Havie sorted old letters by candlelight. Istho walked long way round to avoid muddy square.
